{"description":"Audit UI pages for WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility issues. Produces a structured report with evidence, reproduction steps, and acceptance criteria per issue. Use when asked to audit, check accessibility, or find a11y issues on a page.","instructions":"<skill name="audit-a11y">
# Audit Page for Accessibility

Goal: produce a complete, evidenced WCAG 2.1 AA audit report for the target page.

This skill is outcome-oriented. Adapt to the environment and choose the most direct path to each phase goal. Do not stop between phases unless you hit a blocker you cannot resolve alone.

## Rules of engagement

Read `references/rules-of-engagement.md` before starting — WCAG scope, severity mapping, finding validity, testing requirements, and all nine check categories (6a–6i).

## Workflow

Execute `references/workflow.md`.

High-level (12 phases, 9 check categories):
1. Setup — start the app in sandbox, confirm page loads, record version metadata.
2. Automated scan (6a) — axe-core injection via agent-browser (or pre-built script if available).
3. Semantic structure (6b) — landmarks, headings, lists, tables, language, ARIA relationships.
4. Screen reader experience (6c + 6d) — accessible names, reading order, state announcements, hidden/visible text.
5. Keyboard navigation and traps (6e) — full tab-order mapping, trap detection, keyboard-only operability.
6. Interactive widgets and focus management (6e + 6f) — APG patterns, focus lifecycle on open/close/delete/navigate.
7. Live regions and dynamic content (6g) — status messages, alerts, toasts, loading, SPA navigation.
8. Visual presentation (6h) — color, contrast, target size, motion, reflow.
9. Forms and error handling (6i) — labels, required, autocomplete, error flow, grouping.
10. Evidence capture — screenshots, a11y tree excerpts, keyboard traces. Per-issue folders.
11. Generate root report in `reports/<page-name>/`.
12. Done.

## Pre-built audit scripts

Page-specific scripts may be available under `scripts/`. Use them as a starting point for the automated scan phase:

```bash
cd /path/to/audit-dir
cp /workspace/scripts/audit-chat.js .
cp /workspace/scripts/package.json .
npm install
node audit-chat.js http://localhost:9300 ./output
```

These produce `axe-results.json`, `page-data.json`, `issues.json`, and screenshots. Review the output and supplement with the manual check phases.

## Page-specific checks

See `references/page-checks.md` for additional manual checks specific to known pages.

## Output

```
reports/<page-name>/
├── report.md                    # Root report — summary + issue table with links
├── screenshots/                 # Page-level screenshots (full page, annotated)
└── issues/
    └── <issue-id>/              # One folder per finding (e.g., 01-missing-skip-link)
        ├── report.md            # Full issue report (references/issue-template.md)
        ├── *.png                # Issue-specific screenshots
        └── *                    # Other artifacts (a11y tree dumps, keyboard traces)
```

See `references/report-format.md` for the full report and issue template structure.

## What this skill does NOT do

- Fix issues (output is the report only).
- Create branches or PRs.
- Expand scope beyond the specified page.

</skill>","skill":"audit-a11y"}

2|
3|How to get Everruns running inside a sandbox for self-contained auditing.
4|
5|## Goal
6|
7|Everruns UI is running at `http://localhost:9300` inside the sandbox, with browser tooling installed and ready to audit.
8|
9|## Preferred: Use the pre-built snapshot
10|
11|Create the sandbox with snapshot `everruns-a11y-nanny`. This snapshot has the full toolchain, Everruns repo, browser automation, and Chromium pre-installed.
12|
13|```
14|daytona_create_sandbox  size=large  snapshot=everruns-a11y-nanny  auto_stop_minutes=30
15|```
16|
17|After creation, read `/home/daytona/SANDBOX.md` inside the sandbox for details on what's installed and where.
18|
19|Then start Everruns:
20|
21|```bash
22|cd /home/daytona/everruns/everruns
23|just start-dev --no-watch
24|```
25|
26|Poll `http://localhost:9300` until it responds. Done.
27|
28|**If the snapshot is unavailable** (deleted, quota exceeded, region mismatch), fall back to the manual setup below.
29|
30|## Fallback: Manual setup
31|
32|### Disk
33|
34|Request **10 GiB disk** — the full stack (Rust toolchain + repo + node_modules + Chromium) needs ~5 GB.
35|
36|### Step 1 — Toolchain
37|
38|The sandbox needs: Rust (recent stable), `just`, `caddy`, and Node.js/npm.
39|
40|- Prefer `apt` for caddy and Node.js
41|- For Rust, the system `apt` version may be too old. If `cargo install just` fails with compilation errors, install a recent Rust via rustup: `https://static.rust-lang.org/rustup/dist/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rustup-init`
42|- Use `sudo` for system package installs
43|
44|Done when: `rustc --version`, `just --version`, `caddy version`, `node --version` all succeed.
45|
46|### Step 2 — Clone and start Everruns
47|
48|- Clone `https://github.com/everruns/everruns.git` into the sandbox
49|- Install UI dependencies: `npm install --omit=dev` in `apps/ui/`
50|- Start in dev mode: `just start-dev --no-watch`
51|- Poll `http://localhost:9300` until it responds
52|
53|Dev mode uses in-memory storage — no database or external services needed. No authentication required.
54|
55|Done when: `curl -sf http://localhost:9300` succeeds.
56|

58|
59|```bash
60|npm install -g agent-browser
61|npx playwright install chromium
62|```
63|
64|> **Package name:** The npm package is `agent-browser` (unscoped). Do NOT use `@agentdesk/agent-browser` — that does not exist.

{"content":"1|# Rules of Engagement — A11y Audit
2|
3|Rules and criteria the agent follows when auditing a page. Referenced from `SKILL.md` and `references/workflow.md`.
4|
5|## 1. WCAG scope
6|
7|We test against WCAG 2.0, 2.1, and 2.2 — all three conformance levels:
8|
9|| Level | Treatment |
10||-------|-----------|
11|| **A** | Mandatory. Every violation is a finding. |
12|| **AA** | Mandatory. Every violation is a finding. |
13|| **AAA** | Advisory. Report but tag as AAA — these are recommendations, not blockers. |
14|| **Best practices** | Advisory. Report separately from WCAG violations. |
15|
16|Every finding must cite the **specific WCAG success criterion** (e.g., 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, Level A) — not just an axe-core rule ID.
17|
18|## 2. Severity mapping
19|
20|We use four severity levels, aligned with axe-core's `impact` but refined by manual judgment:
21|
22|| Severity | Definition | axe `impact` mapping |
23||----------|-----------|---------------------|
24|| **Critical** | Blocks access entirely for one or more disability groups. Unusable. | critical |
25|| **Serious** | Major barrier. Workaround may exist but is unreasonable. | serious |
26|| **Moderate** | Causes difficulty. Workaround exists. | moderate |
27|| **Minor** | Inconvenience or suboptimal experience. Cosmetic a11y. | minor |
28|
29|Axe severity is a starting point — override when manual testing reveals higher/lower real-world impact.
30|
31|## 3. Finding validity
32|
33|A finding is valid when:
34|- It is **reproducible** in the audit environment.
35|- It maps to a **specific WCAG success criterion** (or is tagged as best-practice).
36|- It affects **real user interaction**, not just static analysis noise.
37|
38|**Not** a finding:
39|- Browser-only rendering artifacts not present in production.
40|- Third-party widgets fully outside the application's control (document as "out of scope" if observed).
41|
42|When uncertain, include the finding with a caveat noting the uncertainty.
43|
44|## 4. Testing requirements
45|
46|### 4a. Page readiness — fully loaded, error-free
47|
48|Before any check, screenshot, or evidence capture: **verify the page is fully loaded and shows real content.**
49|
50|1. Wait for network idle (`agent-browser wait --load networkidle`).
51|2. Check for error states — crash overlays, error boundaries, blank pages, HMR errors, auth redirects, permission-denied pages. If any are present, **stop and resolve before continuing**. Audit results from a broken page are invalid.
52|3. Confirm main content is rendered — not a loading spinner, skeleton screen, or empty state caused by a failed API call.
53|4. After every navigation or interaction that changes the page, re-verify readiness before taking screenshots or capturing evidence.
54|5. If readiness cannot be achieved, document it as a blocker in the report and do not audit that page state.
55|
56|This applies globally — every screenshot, every axe-core scan, every snapshot, every keyboard test must run against a **fully loaded, error-free page**.
57|
58|### 4b. Test, don't guess
59|
60|Every finding must be backed by **evidence** obtained during the audit:
61|- axe-core violation output
62|- accessibility tree snapshot showing the issue
63|- keyboard navigation observation (focus trap, missing indicator, wrong order)
64|- screenshot showing the problem state
65|
66|Do not report issues based on code reading or assumptions. If agent-browser can't verify it, note the limitation explicitly.
67|
68|### 4c. Multiple states
69|
70|Where practical, test multiple states of the page:
71|- Default / loaded state
72|- Empty state (if achievable)
73|- With interactive widgets open (dropdowns, filters, modals, menus)
74|- After user actions (sorting, filtering, creating entries)
75|
76|## 5. Analysis principle
77|
78|**Analyze, don't checklist.** Each check category is a lens for deep investigation, not a list of boxes to tick. The goal is to reason about what a real user — blind, low-vision, motor-impaired, cognitive — would actually experience. If something is technically valid ARIA but would confuse a VoiceOver user navigating by rotor, it's a finding. If tab order is "logical" but forces 47 stops before reaching the main content, it's a finding. Surface every issue that degrades real-world usability, even when no single WCAG SC is cleanly violated — report those as best-practice findings.
79|
80|## 6. What to check
81|
82|Nine categories. Run all of them on every audit.
83|
84|### 6a. Automated scan (axe-core)
85|
86|Inject axe-core via `agent-browser eval`. Run with tags: `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag2aaa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`, `best-practice`. Record all violations and incomplete checks.
87|
88|Axe is the floor, not the ceiling. Most categories below catch issues axe cannot.
89|
90|### 6b. Semantic structure
91|
92|Inspect the accessibility tree (`agent-browser snapshot`) for correct document semantics.
93|
94|- **Landmarks** — `main`, `banner`, `navigation`, `contentinfo` present. No duplicate `main`. All visible content within a landmark. Landmarks have accessible names when multiples of the same type exist.
95|- **Headings** — single `h1`. No skipped levels. Headings describe their sections. Heading hierarchy matches visual hierarchy.
96|- **Lists** — related items use `<ul>`/`<ol>`/`<dl>`, not styled `<div>`s.
97|- **Tables** — data tables have `<caption>` or `aria-label`. `<th>` with `scope`. Layout tables marked with `role="presentation"`.
98|- **Language** — `lang` attribute on `<html>`. Language changes within content marked with `lang` on the element (WCAG 3.1.1, 3.1.2).
99|- **Content relationships** — `aria-describedby`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-owns` point to existing IDs. No broken references.
100|
101|### 6c. Screen reader experience
102|
103|Test what screen reader users would hear. The accessibility tree from `agent-browser snapshot` is the same data AT consumes.
104|
105|#### Reading order
106|- Walk the accessibility tree top-to-bottom. Does the content order match the visual layout?
107|- Visually adjacent but DOM-distant elements — would a SR user find them together?
108|
109|#### Accessible names and descriptions
110|- Every interactive element must have a non-empty, meaningful accessible name.
111|- `aria-label` must not conflict with visible text (Label in Name, WCAG 2.5.3).
112|- `aria-describedby` for supplementary info — verify referenced elements exist and contain useful text.
113|
114|#### State announcements
115|- Interact with expandable/selectable/toggleable elements via keyboard. Re-snapshot and verify `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, `aria-checked`, `aria-pressed` changed correctly.
116|- Disabled state — `aria-disabled` or `disabled` attribute, not just visual graying.
117|
118|### 6d. Accessible names and text
119|
120|Deep inspection of text content available to assistive technology vs what's visible.
121|
122|- **Visually hidden text** — sr-only/clip patterns. Present where needed? Absent where it would create noise?
123|- **Truncated text** — is the full text available to AT?
124|- **CSS-generated content** — `::before`/`::after` with meaningful `content`. Verify informational text is in the accessible name.
125|- **Placeholder-as-label** — inputs with `placeholder` but no `<label>` or `aria-label`.
126|- **Icon-only elements** — buttons or links containing only an icon. Must have `aria-label` or sr-only text.
127|- **Empty interactive elements** — links or buttons with no accessible name.
128|
129|### 6e. Keyboard navigation and traps
130|
131|Full keyboard-only operability. Use `agent-browser press Tab`, `press Shift+Tab`, `press Enter`, `press Escape`, `press ArrowDown`, etc.
132|
133|- **Tab order mapping** — tab through entire page, record each stop. Order must follow visual reading order.
134|- **Tab stop count** — if reaching main content requires many stops, a skip link or landmark nav is needed.
135|- **Focus visibility** — every focusable element shows a visible focus indicator. Focus indicator contrast at least 3:1 (WCAG 2.4.11).
136|- **Keyboard traps** — at every focusable element, verify Tab and Shift+Tab move focus away. Special attention to rich editors, iframes, custom widgets, modals.
137|- **Skip link** — present, visible on focus, moves focus to main content.
138|- **All functionality reachable** — every mouse action must have a keyboard alternative.
139|- **Widget keyboard patterns** (WAI-ARIA APG): tabs, menus, comboboxes, dialogs, accordions, trees — test against expected patterns.
140|
141|### 6f. Focus management
142|
143|Focus lifecycle during dynamic interactions.
144|
145|- **SPA route changes** — focus moves to new content heading or main area, not lost to `<body>`.
146|- **Modal/dialog open** — focus moves into dialog. Background content is inert.
147|- **Modal/dialog close** — focus returns to trigger element.
148|- **Content removal** — after delete, focus moves to a logical successor, not `<body>`.
149|- **Form submission** — focus moves to success/error message or next step.
150|- **Tabindex audit** — no positive `tabindex` values. `tabindex="-1"` only on programmatic focus targets. `tabindex="0"` only on non-natively-focusable elements that need tab access.
151|
152|### 6g. Live regions and dynamic content
153|
154|The #1 category axe-core cannot catch.
155|
156|- **Status messages** (WCAG 4.1.3) — loading indicators, save confirmations, filter counts. Must use `role="status"` or `aria-live="polite"`.
157|- **Alerts** — error messages, validation failures. Must use `role="alert"` or `aria-live="assertive"`.
158|- **Toast/notification** — must be announced. Auto-dismiss must give enough time (WCAG 2.2.1).
159|- **Loading states** — AT users need to know content is loading and when it's done. Check for `aria-busy="true"` or `role="status"`.
160|- **SPA navigation** — route changes must announce new page via live region, focus management, or title change.
161|
162|### 6h. Visual presentation
163|
164|- **Color as sole indicator** — information conveyed only by color (WCAG 1.4.1).
165|- **Focus indicator contrast** — at least 3:1 against adjacent background (WCAG 2.4.11).
166|- **Target size** — interactive elements at least 24x24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8 AA). Note elements < 44x44 (WCAG 2.5.5 AAA).
167|- **Motion** — check for `prefers-reduced-motion` support. No auto-playing animations without pause control.
168|- **Text spacing** — inject spacing overrides, verify content remains usable (WCAG 1.4.12).
169|- **Reflow** — test at 320px width, flag horizontal scrolling (WCAG 1.4.10).
170|
171|### 6i. Forms and error handling
172|
173|- **Label association** — every input has a programmatically associated label. Accessible name matches visible label.
174|- **Required fields** — `required` or `aria-required`, not just visual asterisk.
175|- **Input purpose** — common inputs have `autocomplete` attribute (WCAG 1.3.5).
176|- **Error identification** — errors described in text, associated to inputs via `aria-describedby`/`aria-errormessage`.
177|- **Error focus** — on validation failure, focus moves to first error or error summary.
178|- **Validation timing** — aggressive on-change validation noted as potential SR issue.
179|- **Grouping** — related controls in `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` or `role="group"` with name.
180|
181|## 7. Scope discipline
182|
183|- Audit only the **page/view specified** per audit run.
184|- Note issues in shared components (header, nav) but attribute them correctly.
185|- Do not attempt fixes. Do not create branches or PRs. Output is the report only.
186|- Do not expand scope mid-audit. {"content":"1|# Audit A11y — Workflow
2|
3|> Read `references/rules-of-engagement.md` first — WCAG scope, severity mapping, finding validity, all nine check categories (6a–6i).
4|
5|## Phase 1: Setup
6|
7|**Goal:** Correct audit environment ready, page fully loaded and error-free, metadata captured.
8|
9|- Start the application in the sandbox environment per `specs/sandbox-setup.md`.
10|- Capture version metadata: short commit SHA, branch, commit date.
11|- **Page readiness gate** (rules-of-engagement §4a):
12|  - Open page in agent-browser. Wait for network idle (`wait --load networkidle`).
13|  - Verify no error overlays, crash boundaries, blank pages, HMR errors, auth redirects, or permission-denied fallbacks.
14|  - Confirm main content is fully rendered — not a spinner, skeleton, or empty state from a failed request.
15|  - If page is broken, fix before proceeding. Do not audit a half-loaded or error page.
16|- Create report output dir: `reports/<page-name>/` with `screenshots/` and `issues/` subdirs.
17|
18|**Done when:** page fully loaded and error-free in agent-browser, metadata recorded.
19|
20|## Phase 2: Automated scan (category 6a)
21|
22|**Goal:** Machine-detectable WCAG violations captured.
23|
24|- Run the pre-built audit script if available for this page (`scripts/audit-chat.js` for /chat).
25|- Otherwise inject axe-core via `agent-browser eval`, run full scan covering `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag2aaa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`, `best-practice`.
26|- Collect violations (with impact, WCAG tags, affected nodes) and incomplete checks.
27|- Record pass/inapplicable counts for methodology section.
28|
29|**Done when:** axe-core results recorded. This is the floor — most issues come from phases below.
30|
31|## Phase 3: Semantic structure (category 6b)
32|
33|**Goal:** Accessibility tree matches semantic expectations.
34|
35|Take `agent-browser snapshot`. Analyze the full tree for:
36|
37|- Landmarks — presence, uniqueness, naming, all content within a landmark.
38|- Headings — hierarchy, single h1, descriptive text, no skips.
39|- Lists and tables — correct semantic markup, table headers with scope.
40|- Language — `lang` on `<html>`, language changes on inline content.
41|- ARIA relationships — `aria-describedby`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-owns` reference valid IDs.
42|
43|**Done when:** structural findings documented with a11y tree excerpts as evidence.
44|
45|## Phase 4: Screen reader experience (categories 6c + 6d)
46|
47|**Goal:** What screen reader users would hear is correct, complete, and usable.
48|
49|Use `agent-browser snapshot` for the a11y tree. Use `agent-browser eval` to query computed accessible names, ARIA attributes, hidden text, and CSS-generated content.
50|
51|### Accessible names and text (6d)
52|- Walk every interactive element in the a11y tree. Flag missing, empty, generic, or conflicting accessible names.
53|- Check for visually hidden sr-only text — present where needed? absent where it would create noise?
54|- Check truncated text, placeholder-as-label, icon-only elements, CSS-generated content.
55|- Verify `aria-label` does not conflict with visible text (Label in Name, WCAG 2.5.3).
56|
57|### Reading order and structure (6c)
58|- Read the a11y tree top-to-bottom. Does the order match the visual layout?
59|- Check for DOM-order vs visual-order mismatches (flexbox `order`, CSS grid, absolute positioning).
60|
61|### State announcements (6c)
62|- Interact with expandable/selectable/toggleable elements via keyboard.
63|- Re-snapshot after each interaction. Verify `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, `aria-checked`, `aria-pressed` changed correctly.
64|- Check disabled states — `aria-disabled` or `disabled`, not just visual graying.
65|
66|**Done when:** every interactive element's accessible name verified, reading order validated, state changes confirmed.
67|
68|## Phase 5: Keyboard navigation and traps (category 6e)
69|
70|**Goal:** All functionality reachable and operable via keyboard alone, no traps.
71|
72|Use `agent-browser press Tab`, `press Shift+Tab`, `press Enter`, `press Escape`, `press ArrowDown`, etc. Re-snapshot after each key press.
73|
74|- Map the complete tab order. Record each stop.
75|- Count stops to reach main content — flag if excessive (no skip link / landmark nav).
76|- Check focus visibility at every stop (screenshot focus states).
77|- Test for traps at every stop — Tab and Shift+Tab must move focus. Special attention to rich editors, iframes, custom widgets, modals.
78|- Verify skip link existence, visibility on focus, and correct target.
79|- Test all mouse-only interactions for keyboard alternatives.
80|
81|**Done when:** full tab order mapped, every trap tested, keyboard-only operability confirmed or violations documented.
82|
83|## Phase 6: Interactive widgets and focus management (categories 6e + 6f)
84|
85|**Goal:** Widgets follow APG patterns, focus is managed correctly through all lifecycle events.
86|
87|For each interactive widget (tabs, menus, comboboxes, dialogs, accordions, trees, date pickers):
88|
89|### Widget keyboard patterns (6e)
90|- Test keyboard activation (Enter/Space), arrow navigation, Escape to close, Home/End.
91|- Check role and state attributes via snapshot.
92|- Screenshot each state (closed, open, item focused, item selected).
93|
94|### Focus management lifecycle (6f)
95|- **Open**: focus moves into the widget / dialog.
96|- **Close**: focus returns to trigger element.
97|- **Destructive action**: after delete/remove, focus moves to a logical successor (not `<body>`).
98|- **Form submission**: focus moves to success/error message or next step.
99|- **SPA navigation**: focus moves to new content heading or main area.
100|
101|### Tabindex audit (6f)
102|- No positive `tabindex` values anywhere on the page.
103|- `tabindex="-1"` only on programmatic focus targets.
104|- `tabindex="0"` only on non-natively-focusable elements that need tab access.
105|
106|**Done when:** every widget tested against APG patterns, focus lifecycle verified for all dynamic interactions.
107|
108|## Phase 7: Live regions and dynamic content (category 6g)
109|
110|**Goal:** All dynamic content changes are announced to assistive technology.
111|
112|Trigger every dynamic content change on the page and verify announcements:
113|
114|- Loading states — check for `aria-busy` or `role="status"` live region.
115|- Form validation — errors use `role="alert"` or `aria-live="assertive"`. Success uses `role="status"`.
116|- Toast/notification — container is a live region, auto-dismiss allows enough time.
117|- Filter/sort results — count updates use `role="status"` or equivalent.
118|- SPA route changes — new page announced via live region, focus management, or title change.
119|- Inline editing — save confirmation announced.
120|
121|**Technique:** trigger action → `agent-browser diff snapshot` → check for live-region markup on changed/new elements.
122|
123|**Done when:** every dynamic content change tested, live-region usage (or absence) documented.
124|
125|## Phase 8: Visual presentation (category 6h)
126|
127|**Goal:** Visual design does not create barriers.
128|
129|- Color as sole indicator — information conveyed only by color (WCAG 1.4.1).
130|- Focus indicator contrast — at least 3:1 against adjacent background (WCAG 2.4.11).
131|- Target size — measure via `eval` with `getBoundingClientRect()`. Flag elements < 24x24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8 AA). Note < 44x44 (WCAG 2.5.5 AAA).
132|- Motion — check for `prefers-reduced-motion` support. Flag auto-playing animations, flashing content.
133|- Text spacing — inject spacing overrides via `eval` and verify content remains usable (WCAG 1.4.12).
134|- Reflow — test at 320px width via `eval` viewport resize. Flag horizontal scrolling (WCAG 1.4.10).
135|
136|**Done when:** visual barriers documented with screenshots and measurements.
137|
138|## Phase 9: Forms and error handling (category 6i)
139|
140|**Goal:** Forms are fully usable by AT users through all states.
141|
142|If the page contains forms:
143|
144|- Check every input for programmatic label association.
145|- Required fields — `required` or `aria-required`, not just visual asterisk.
146|- `autocomplete` on common inputs (name, email, tel, address fields) — WCAG 1.3.5.
147|- Trigger validation errors. Check: errors described in text, associated to inputs via `aria-describedby`/`aria-errormessage`, focus moves to first error or summary.
148|- Check validation timing — aggressive on-change validation noted as potential SR issue.
149|- Related controls grouped in `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` or `role="group"` with name.
150|
151|**Done when:** form usability for AT verified across all states (empty, filled, error, success).
152|
153|## Phase 10: Evidence capture and issue reports
154|
155|**Goal:** Each finding gets its own folder with evidence and a self-contained report.
156|
157|### Directory structure
158|
159|```
160|reports/<page-name>/
161|├── report.md                          # Root report — aggregation + summary
162|├── screenshots/
163|│   ├── full-page.png                  # Full page screenshot
164|│   └── annotated.png                  # Annotated interactive elements
165|└── issues/
166|    └── <issue-id>/                    # One folder per finding
167|        ├── report.md                  # Full issue report (references/issue-template.md)
168|        ├── <screenshot>.png           # Issue-specific screenshots
169|        └── <artifact>                 # Other evidence (a11y tree dumps, keyboard traces)
170|```
171|
172|### Issue ID convention
173|
174|`<NN>-<short-slug>` — e.g., `01-missing-skip-link`, `02-dialog-no-focus-trap`, `13-status-no-live-region`.
175|
176|### Per-issue folder
177|
178|For each finding:
179|
180|1. Create `issues/<issue-id>/`.
181|2. Save issue-specific screenshots into the folder. **Re-verify page readiness** (§4a) before each capture.
182|3. Save any other evidence (a11y tree excerpts as `.txt`, keyboard traces).
183|4. Write `issues/<issue-id>/report.md` following `references/issue-template.md`.
184|
185|### Page-level screenshots
186|
187|- Full page screenshot → `screenshots/`.
188|- Annotated screenshot (`--annotate`) → `screenshots/`.
189|
190|## Phase 11: Root report
191|
192|**Goal:** Aggregation report linking to all issue reports.
193|
194|Write `reports/<page-name>/report.md` following `references/report-template.md`:
195|
196|- Metadata: URL, version (commit SHA, branch, date), audit date, WCAG standard.
197|- Summary tables — issue counts by severity AND by category (6a–6i).
198|- **Issues table** — one row per finding with: number, title, category, WCAG, severity, affected users, link to `issues/<issue-id>/report.md`.
199|- Axe-core raw results.
200|- Environment caveats.
201|- Methodology with page readiness confirmation, environment, tool versions, and category coverage.
202|
203|**Done when:** `report.md` generated, every issue linked, all issue folders contain their report and evidence.
204|
205|## Phase 12: Done

# Audit Page for Accessibility

Goal: produce a complete, evidenced WCAG 2.1 AA audit report for the target page.

This skill is outcome-oriented. Adapt to the environment and choose the most direct path to each phase goal. Do not stop between phases unless you hit a blocker you cannot resolve alone.

## Rules of engagement

Read `references/rules-of-engagement.md` before starting — WCAG scope, severity mapping, finding validity, testing requirements, and all nine check categories (6a–6i).

## Workflow

Execute `references/workflow.md`.

High-level (12 phases, 9 check categories):
1. Setup — start the app in sandbox, confirm page loads, record version metadata.
2. Automated scan (6a) — axe-core injection via agent-browser (or pre-built script if available).
3. Semantic structure (6b) — landmarks, headings, lists, tables, language, ARIA relationships.
4. Screen reader experience (6c + 6d) — accessible names, reading order, state announcements, hidden/visible text.
5. Keyboard navigation and traps (6e) — full tab-order mapping, trap detection, keyboard-only operability.
6. Interactive widgets and focus management (6e + 6f) — APG patterns, focus lifecycle on open/close/delete/navigate.
7. Live regions and dynamic content (6g) — status messages, alerts, toasts, loading, SPA navigation.
8. Visual presentation (6h) — color, contrast, target size, motion, reflow.
9. Forms and error handling (6i) — labels, required, autocomplete, error flow, grouping.
10. Evidence capture — screenshots, a11y tree excerpts, keyboard traces. Per-issue folders.
11. Generate root report in `reports/<page-name>/`.
12. Done.

## Pre-built audit scripts

Page-specific scripts may be available under `scripts/`. Use them as a starting point for the automated scan phase:

```bash
cd /path/to/audit-dir
cp /workspace/scripts/audit-chat.js .
cp /workspace/scripts/package.json .
npm install
node audit-chat.js http://localhost:9300 ./output
```

These produce `axe-results.json`, `page-data.json`, `issues.json`, and screenshots. Review the output and supplement with the manual check phases.

See `references/page-checks.md` for additional manual checks specific to known pages.

```
        └── *                    # Other artifacts (a11y tree dumps, keyboard traces)
```

See `references/report-format.md` for the full report and issue template structure.

- Fix issues (output is the report only).
- Create branches or PRs.
- Expand scope beyond the specified page.

3|description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction.

6|
7|# Browser Automation with agent-browser
8|
9|The CLI uses Chrome/Chromium via CDP directly. Install via `npm i -g agent-browser`, `brew install agent-browser`, or `cargo install agent-browser`. Run `agent-browser install` to download Chrome. Existing Chrome, Brave, Playwright, and Puppeteer installations are detected automatically. Run `agent-browser upgrade` to update to the latest version.
10|
11|## Core Workflow
12|
13|Every browser automation follows this pattern:
14|
15|1. **Navigate**: `agent-browser open <url>`
16|2. **Snapshot**: `agent-browser snapshot -i` (get element refs like `@e1`, `@e2`)
17|3. **Interact**: Use refs to click, fill, select
18|4. **Re-snapshot**: After navigation or DOM changes, get fresh refs
19|
20|```bash
21|agent-browser open https://example.com/form
22|agent-browser snapshot -i
23|# Output: @e1 [input type="email"], @e2 [input type="password"], @e3 [button] "Submit"
24|
25|agent-browser fill @e1 "user@example.com"
26|agent-browser fill @e2 "password123"
27|agent-browser click @e3
28|agent-browser wait --load networkidle
29|agent-browser snapshot -i  # Check result
30|```
31|
32|## Command Chaining
33|
34|Commands can be chained with `&&` in a single shell invocation. The browser persists between commands via a background daemon, so chaining is safe and more efficient than separate calls.
35|
36|```bash
37|# Chain open + wait + snapshot in one call
38|agent-browser open https://example.com && agent-browser wait --load networkidle && agent-browser snapshot -i
39|
40|# Chain multiple interactions
41|agent-browser fill @e1 "user@example.com" && agent-browser fill @e2 "password123" && agent-browser click @e3
42|
43|# Navigate and capture
44|agent-browser open https://example.com && agent-browser wait --load networkidle && agent-browser screenshot page.png
45|```
46|
47|**When to chain:** Use `&&` when you don't need to read the output of an intermediate command before proceeding (e.g., open + wait + screenshot). Run commands separately when you need to parse the output first (e.g., snapshot to discover refs, then interact using those refs).
48|
49|## Handling Authentication
50|
51|When automating a site that requires login, choose the approach that fits:
52|
53|**Option 1: Import auth from the user's browser (fastest for one-off tasks)**
54|
55|```bash
56|# Connect to the user's running Chrome (they're already logged in)
57|agent-browser --auto-connect state save ./auth.json
58|# Use that auth state
59|agent-browser --state ./auth.json open https://app.example.com/dashboard
60|```
61|
62|State files contain session tokens in plaintext -- add to `.gitignore` and delete when no longer needed. Set `AGENT_BROWSER_ENCRYPTION_KEY` for encryption at rest.
63|
64|**Option 2: Chrome profile reuse (zero setup)**
65|
66|```bash
67|# List available Chrome profiles
68|agent-browser profiles
69|
70|# Reuse the user's existing Chrome login state
71|agent-browser --profile Default open https://gmail.com
72|```
73|

75|

77|# First run: login manually or via automation
78|agent-browser --profile ~/.myapp open https://app.example.com/login
79|# ... fill credentials, submit ...
80|
81|# All future runs: already authenticated
82|agent-browser --profile ~/.myapp open https://app.example.com/dashboard
83|```
84|
85|**Option 4: Session name (auto-save/restore cookies + localStorage)**
86|

88|agent-browser --session-name myapp open https://app.example.com/login

92|# Next time: state auto-restored

97|

101|```
